To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adding a small amount of MgCl2 to a solution of NaCl leads to sharp condensation and to polarization of the Mg(2+)-ion cluster near the phosphate groups, that this leads to a significant increase in the DNA-DN interaction energy, that these effects can be described by the epsilon-MPB model, and that the epsilon-MPB calculations are in good agreement with the experimental data.

the epsilon-modified Poissons-Boltzmann theory is able to describe the effect of multivalent cation Mg(2+) on the electrostatic interaction between two B-DNA molecules in a mixture of Na(+) and Mg(2+) ions.

the epsilon-MPB theory, which is based on the assumption that the dielectric saturation effects in the first hydration shell of ions are described in terms of the effective ion-ion interactions, is capable of describing the ionic distributions around the DNA molecule and the DNA-DNA interactions in a mixture of Na(+) and Mg(2+) ions in solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of multivalent ions (Mg(2+)) in the electrostatics of nucleic acids in physiological solutions.

the development of a novel theoretical approach to the description of the ionic distributions and of the interaction energies of charged macromolecules in the solutions of multivalent cation mixtures.
the development of the theory for ionic interactions in aqueous solution of arbitrary mixture of ions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epsilon-MPB model is able to describe the mediating role played by multivalent cations and their effect on DNA electrostatics.
the epsilon-MPB model of ionic solutions is a useful tool for the description of ionic distribution and electrostatics of DNA in the presence of divalent cationic impurities.
the multivalent cations are important for the DNA-DNA interactions, and the epsilon-MPB approach is able to capture the essential features of this effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dielectric saturation effects and the ion-ion interactions in the mixture of monovalent and divalent ions play an important role in the electrostatics of DNA in physiological solutions.
the epsilon-MPB theory is capable of describing the ionic distributions in the vicinity of DNA and the B-DNA-DNA interaction energies in a mixture of Na(+), Mg(2+), and Cl(-) ions.

the epsilon-MPB model is able to describe the ionic distributions around the DNA and the DNA-DNA interactions in solutions of the arbitrary mixture of NaCl, MgCl(2), and CaCl(2) in a good agreement with the all-atom MD simulation results.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MPB approach with the epsilon parameter is capable of describing the ionic distributions around a macromolecule in solution of a multicomponent electrolyte and of calculating the DNA-DNA interactions in such electrolytes.
dielectric saturation is a key effect that should be taken into account for a proper description of DNA electrostatics in multivalent solutions.
the dielectric saturation effects should not be neglected while calculating ionic distribution and interaction energies in DNA electrostatic calculations.
